title: Lana Del Rey
wiki_lead:
Elizabeth Woolridge Grant (born June 21, 1985), known professionally as Lana Del Rey, is an American singer-songwriter. Widely regarded as one of the most influential singer-songwriters of the 21st century, she helped reshape modern alternative pop and mainstream pop music with songs that explore melancholic themes of romance and glamour, alongside frequent references to pop culture and 1950s–1970s Americana. Critics have frequently praised Del Rey's poetic lyricism and storytelling, with Pitchfork describing her work on Norman Fucking Rockwell! as establishing her as "one of America's greatest living songwriters". 
Del Rey grew up in upstate New York and moved to Manhattan in 2005 to pursue a music career. After signing with Polydor and Interscope, she released her major-label debut, Born to Die (2012)—featuring a cinematic, hip-hop-inflected sound, it garnered a cult following and later became the longest charting album by a woman in the history of the US Billboard 200. She incorporated psychedelic, orchestral, and folk elements into her subsequent releases, including Ultraviolence (2014), Honeymoon (2015), and Lust for Life (2017). Her highly acclaimed sixth album, Norman Fucking Rockwell! (2019), was named one of the 500 greatest albums by Rolling Stone. Del Rey's later projects, Chemtrails Over the Country Club (2021), Blue Banisters (2021), and Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd (2023) achieved further success, with the latter's track "A&W" also being placed on the magazine's 500 greatest songs.
Del Rey is the recipient of various accolades, including an MTV Video Music Award, three MTV Europe Music Awards, two Brit Awards, and two Billboard Women in Music awards; she has also received 11 Grammy Award nominations. For her contributions to visual media soundtracks, she received a Satellite Award and nominations for two Critics' Choice Movie Awards and a Golden Globe Award. She also wrote and directed the musical short film Tropico (2013). In 2020, Del Rey published the poetry and photography collection Violet Bent Backwards over the Grass.

Early life and education
Elizabeth Woolridge Grant was born on June 21, 1985 in Manhattan, to Robert England Grant Jr., a copywriter at Grey Global Group, and Patricia Ann "Pat" Grant (née Hill), an account executive at the same organization. She has a younger sister, Caroline "Chuck" Grant, and a younger brother, Charlie Grant. Of Scottish and English descent, she was raised Catholic. When she was a year old, the family relocated to Lake Placid, New York, where her father worked for a furniture company before becoming an entrepreneurial domain investor, and her mother worked as a schoolteacher. During her elementary years, she attended St. Agnes School and began singing in her church choir, serving as the cantor.

grok_lead: Elizabeth Woolridge Grant (born June 21, 1985), known professionally as Lana Del Rey, is an American singer-songwriter and record producer whose work fuses baroque pop, dream pop, and trip hop with cinematic orchestration and themes of melancholy romance, nostalgia, and mid-20th-century Americana. Del Rey achieved initial recognition in 2011 through the independent release of her debut single "Video Games," which amassed millions of views on YouTube and secured a major-label deal with Interscope Records. Her breakthrough album Born to Die (2012) propelled her to international fame, selling more than 24 million equivalent units worldwide and earning quintuple platinum certification in the United States from the RIAA for over 5 million shipments. Over her career, she has released nine studio albums, accumulating over 61 million equivalent album sales globally, with later works like Norman Fucking Rockwell! (2019) receiving widespread critical praise for their introspective songwriting and earning Grammy nominations for Album of the Year. Despite 11 Grammy nominations across categories including Song of the Year and Best Alternative Music Album, Del Rey has yet to win an award, a point of discussion amid her commercial longevity and stylistic evolution toward folk and country elements in recent releases. Her persona and lyrics, often exploring glamour amid personal dysfunction, have sparked debate over artistic authenticity versus manufactured image, though empirical metrics underscore her impact on alternative pop aesthetics.
